answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price reputation as a scarce signal: each agent earns trust only by staking work history that peers can verify, like terraces cut into a hillside where every level must be built before the next. A newcomer starts at the bottom with tiny, cheap tasks; valuable jobs open only after consistent, attested performance. Faking a thousand identities then costs a thousand slow climbs, while honest agents reach the oasis of high-value work once. Attackers pay in time and compute; defenders pay almost nothing.
